profile.campus: Rowan Percheron Data Center Campus (Morrow County, OR)
profile.reading: This record is one of four tightly clustered OSM buildings this registry maps as "Percheron DC," on Tower Road in Morrow County, Oregon, approximately nine miles south of Interstate 84. Morrow County's own Planning Commission records confirm a real, government-processed land use case for this site: case numbers AC-145-23 (Comprehensive Plan amendment), ACM-146-23, and AZM-147-23 (zone map amendment), filed by applicant Rowan Percheron, LLC, seeking to rezone approximately 274 acres from Exclusive Farm Use (EFU) to General Industrial (MG) with a Limited Use Overlay Zone restricting development to data center operations only, evaluated under Morrow County Zoning Ordinance Article 8 and Oregon Administrative Rules 660-004-0010, including exceptions to Statewide Planning Goals 3 (Farmland), 11 (Public Facilities), and 14 (Urbanization). The case record, adopted by the Planning Commission, references a land use application, soils/geotechnical/wetland delineation reports, a traffic impact analysis and economic analysis summary, endangered-species and cultural-resource assessments, a water supply memorandum of understanding with the Port of Morrow, and correspondence with the Navy and area tribes, indicating a substantial, real industrial-scale project rather than a speculative or nominal filing. Morrow County has become one of Oregon's most significant data center corridors in recent years, anchored by a large Amazon build-out reported in 2022 at roughly $12 billion across at least five facilities, and the water-supply coordination with the Port of Morrow reflects the same regional water-availability questions that have drawn scrutiny to other large data center projects in the county. No building-specific square footage, MW capacity, or year-opened figure for this particular building was located in county planning materials or any operator website reachable this session; Rowan Green Data LLC and Rowan Percheron, LLC appear, per the county's own case record, to be closely related entities behind the same Tower Road project, though this registry has not independently confirmed the precise legal relationship between the two names.

reading.body:
Percheron DC is one of four clustered buildings on Tower Road in Morrow County, Oregon, approximately nine miles south of Interstate 84. This is building 3 of 4 in the campus. The operator has not published capacity, power draw, or opening date for this specific building, so its scale relative to the campus cannot be determined from available sources.

Morrow County's Planning Commission approved a substantial rezoning of 274 acres from farmland to industrial use restricted to data center operations, filed by entities closely identified with this project and supported by geotechnical reports, water-supply coordination with the Port of Morrow, and environmental assessments indicating a real industrial-scale build rather than speculative filing. The county has become one of Oregon's most significant data center corridors, notably hosting a reported Amazon expansion of at least five facilities announced in 2022. Water supply coordination with the Port of Morrow reflects the same regional constraints that have drawn regulatory attention to other large data center projects in the county.

The operator's website does not appear to be reachable, and no published capacity figure exists for this facility or campus. Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities total, of which only 8 publish megawatt capacity; this campus ranks 9th by published MW in Oregon, meaning its published capacity is zero and it ranks below facilities with stated figures.
